claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin film on a steel substrate.
The as-deposited coating has a relatively coarse grain structure.
The proposed intervention is pre-annealing at 600°C for 1 hour followed by controlled cooling.
Controlled cooling prevents grain coarsening after annealing.
The pre-annealing treatment creates a refined, ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer.
Thermal pre-annealing induces dynamic recrystallization in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
A stable ultra-nanocrystalline tribolayer forms at the coating surface.
The thermal treatment promotes grain-boundary sliding.
Dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding produce a self-adapted tribolayer.
The refined tribolayer accommodates deformation and dissipates mechanical stress during high-temperature sliding.
The refined tribolayer retards microcrack initiation and propagation.
Retarded crack initiation and propagation reduce coating wear.
Pre-annealed coatings will have a statistically significant reduction in wear rate relative to as-deposited coatings.
Improved wear resistance will correlate with a homogeneous ultra-refined nanostructured tribolayer and improved mechanical integrity.
The proposed applicability boundary is 600–700°C and a contact load around 50 N.
Behavior may differ outside the specified temperature and loading range.

contradictions.description: The intervention says pre-wear annealing is intended to create the ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer, whereas the mediator is called a tribolayer and the mechanism describes it as self-adapted through recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding during wear. It is therefore unclear whether the key layer exists before sliding or forms dynamically during sliding.
